content.text: I couldn't see the body of `AuthService.refreshToken`, so this diagnosis is inferred from the bug report and the function's location. I haven't confirmed it against the code.

candidates.explanation: Refresh tokens are tied to a session through a `hash` claim. Rotation only works if `refreshToken` compares `data.hash` with the stored `session.hash` and rejects a mismatch. It must then generate a new random hash, save it on the session, and put that hash into the new tokens. The report says a replayed token still yields a fresh pair. That suggests one of three things: the hash comparison is missing or wrong, the new hash is never saved, or the old hash is reused when the tokens are built. I couldn't see the body, so this is my best guess.

This builds the refresh JWT from the `hash` it is given. If `refreshToken` passes the old `session.hash` instead of the newly generated one, the new refresh token carries the same hash as the old one. The old token then stays valid after rotation.

This only checks that the payload has a sessionId. It does no session or hash check, so a replayed token passes at the guard. Rejecting rotated tokens therefore depends entirely on `AuthService.refreshToken`.

fix.description: In `refreshToken`, load the session by `data.sessionId`. Throw UnauthorizedException if the session is missing or `session.hash !== data.hash`. Then generate a new random hash (for example `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex')`) and persist it on the session with `sessionService.update`. Pass that new hash to `getTokensData`. The old refresh token's hash then no longer matches, so a replay is rejected.

It must then generate a new random hash, save it on the session, and put that hash into the new tokens. The report says a replayed token still yields a fresh pair. This builds the refresh JWT from the `hash` it is given. If `refreshToken` passes the old `session.hash` instead of the newly generated one, the new refresh token carries the same hash as the old one. The old token then stays valid after rotation.

This only checks that the payload has a sessionId. It does no session or hash check, so a replayed token passes at the guard. Rejecting rotated tokens therefore depends entirely on `AuthService.refreshToken`.

fix.description: In `refreshToken`, load the session by `data.sessionId`. Throw UnauthorizedException if the session is missing or `session.hash !== data.hash`. Then generate a new random hash (for example `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex')`) and persist it on the session with `sessionService.update`. Pass that new hash to `getTokensData`. The old refresh token's hash then no longer matches, so a replay is rejected.
